snippet.title: WWII Testimony
snippet.description:
⭐ When World War II ended, the questions began.

American officers sat across the table from Göring, Speer, Dönitz, Rundstedt and the men who had run Germany's war, and asked them what really happened. Hundreds of thousands of German prisoners of war crossed the Atlantic and saw America with their own eyes. Their answers were short, surprising, and rarely what you would expect.

WWII Testimony tells these stories in their own words: one question, one answer, and the history behind it. Every video is built on documented sources: Allied interrogation reports, postwar testimony, memoirs and records, checked against what actually happened. The footage is real archival film from the 1940s.

New videos every day.

snippet.title: They Asked Rundstedt Why D-Day Worked. He Said Two Words, Three Times.
snippet.description:
After the war, British interrogators asked Field Marshal Gerd von Rundstedt why D-Day succeeded. His answer used the same two words three times: air power. This documentary compares his postwar testimony with the official records of Normandy.

We examine the bombing of the Seine bridges, the destruction of German rail traffic, the ordeal of Panzer Lehr, and the morning of June 6, 1944, when two panzer divisions waited for Hitler's permission to move while the clouds still covered Normandy.

What Rundstedt said, what the records show, and what he left out. Subscribe to WWII Testimony for more accounts from the other side, in their own words.

snippet.title: They Asked Speer Which Bombing Raid Hurt Germany Most. He Named One Day.
snippet.description:
In May 1945, American investigators questioned Albert Speer, Hitler's armaments minister, and asked which Allied bombing hurt Germany most. His answer pointed to one day: May 12, 1944, when American bombers struck Germany's synthetic fuel plants.

This documentary follows the interrogation at Glucksburg, the oil campaign pushed by General Carl Spaatz, Speer's warnings to Hitler, the collapse of German fuel output and the shortages that crippled the Luftwaffe and the panzers by December 1944. It also examines why Speer's testimony deserves caution.

Subscribe to WWII Testimony for more accounts of what leaders on the other side said in their own words.

snippet.title: They Asked Göring When He Knew the Luftwaffe Was Finished. He Named One City.
snippet.description:
In May 1945, American air generals interrogated Hermann Göring and asked when he knew the Luftwaffe had lost control of the air. His answer was one German city: Hanover. This documentary follows the Göring interrogation by Carl Spaatz, the arrival of long-range American escort fighters, and what the Reichsmarschall admitted about oil, pilots and production.

We trace the daylight bombing campaign of 1943, the Schweinfurt raid, Goebbels's diary entries, the Aachen order given to Adolf Galland, and the rise of the P-51 Mustang over Berlin in 1944. Every detail comes from interrogation records, memoirs and documented history.

Watch to the end for the missing paragraph that de Seversky said General Arnold left out of his memoirs. Subscribe to WWII Testimony for more firsthand accounts of the war.
